platforms.name: Northflank Cloud Harness
platforms.summary: MicroVM-isolated cloud workspaces preconfigured for a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Devin CLI or OMP) or as an empty sandbox for any agent, on Northflank's cloud or in your own cloud account, with a web terminal, SSH/IDE access and a persistent /home/harness workspace.

byoc.value: Yes, self-serve: AWS, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, GCP, Azure, Oracle, Civo, CoreWeave, Nebius; or import your own Kubernetes cluster (BYOK)
byoc.detail: Northflank provisions and manages the cluster in your account, on the provider's managed Kubernetes service (EKS, GKE, AKS, OKE, Civo Kubernetes, CKS, Nebius Managed Kubernetes). Harnesses need nodes that support a microVM runtime (Kata Containers).

Memory $ 0.00833 / GB / hour
Disk $ 0.15 / GB / month

Devin CLI and OMP harness types are documented in the create-harness API reference; Northflank's quickstart and product pages will list them in an upcoming docs update.

Some Cloud Harness details here (Kata microVMs, agents continuing to run after you disconnect, branch-scoped git push credentials, and a free-plan harness limit of 1 vCPU / 1 GB) come from Northflank's Cloud Harness product page, which isn't public yet as of 2026-10-19. pricing.conversion_note: Modal prices CPU per physical core per second, and 1 core = 2 vCPU ('The cpu parameter specifies physical CPU cores (1 core = 2 vCPUs)', https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources). Sandbox CPU: $0.00003942/core/s x 3600 = $0.141912/core-hour, divided by 2 = $0.070956/vCPU-hour. Sandbox memory: $0.00000667/GiB/s x 3600 = $0.024012/GiB-hour. For comparison, standard Function rates are $0.04716/core-hour ($0.02358/vCPU-hour) and $0.007992/GiB-hour. Billing is max(request, usage), so the request acts as a floor, with a minimum request of 0.125 core and 128 MiB. Storage is quoted per GiB-month and is used here as per GB-month without conversion. Region selection costs 1.15-1.75x and non-preemptible execution 3x base prices; it is not stated whether these multipliers apply to Sandbox rates.

open_questions: Modal prices CPU per physical core; 1 core = 2 vCPU per Modal's docs, so the per-vCPU rate here is the per-core rate halved.
Billing is max(request, actual usage), so it is modelled like allocated pricing: the request is the floor. A sandbox using more than it requests costs more.
Sandbox rates are about 3x Modal's standard Function rates ($0.0000131/core/s and $0.00000222/GiB/s); only Sandbox rates are used here.
Sandboxes run for at most 24 hours. The always-on scenario assumes you snapshot and restore into a new sandbox every 24 hours, which Modal documents but which isn't free of effort.
